ours-fused.short: Night School's attention emulator and kernels, built for this film
ours-fused.citation: media/school/fused/facts.json, written by tools/school/fill_fused.mjs from system/school/fused*.mjs: online softmax and tiled attention checked against a float64 reference on random inputs and the attention model's own Q, K and V; WGSL kernels for the lab; an exact emulator of global memory traffic for unfused and fused attention at N = 64 to 4,096, d = 16 and 64; a broken-rescale control; the overflow arithmetic.
claims: N 4,096: d 64 unfused 514 MiB against fused 258 MiB; d 16, 272.5 against 16.5.
The broken rescale fails on all four probe heads.
Probe row largest score 10.32, exp 30,320 in fp16; on held-out rows the largest score is 23.41.
ours-fused.n: Exact counts; 256 held-out rows for the overflow check.
ours-fused.does_not_prove: Any timing; caches and arithmetic cost are not modelled.

flash2022.citation: Dao, T., Fu, D. Y., Ermon, S., Rudra, A., Re, C. (2022). FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness. NeurIPS 2022. arXiv:2205.14135.
claims: Tiling with the online softmax avoids writing the N x N attention matrix to high-bandwidth memory; Theorem 2 gives O(N^2 d^2 / M) memory accesses.

milakov2018.short: Milakov and Gimelshein 2018, Online normalizer calculation for softmax
milakov2018.citation: Milakov, M., Gimelshein, N. (2018). Online normalizer calculation for softmax. arXiv:1805.02867.
claims: The softmax normaliser can be computed in one pass with a running maximum and a rescaled running sum.
